It constructs a local coordinate system at the surface point $q = p + d(p, v)v$ by choosing two tangent vectors $t_x, t_y \in T_q(S)$ such that $||t_\alpha||_2 = 1$ and $t_x^T t_y = 0$.
The metric tensor (first fundamental form) is $g_{ij} = \partial_i S^T \partial_j S = \delta_{ij} + c_i c_j + c_i v_0^T t_j + c_j v_0^T t_i$, where $c_k = \nabla_p d t_k$.
In theory, since $\nabla_p d$ is parallel to normal $n$ and orthogonal to tangents, $c_x = c_y = 0$, so $g_{ij} = \delta_{ij}$.
It is used in inverse rendering pipelines to prepare point clouds for splatting-based rendering and relighting.
